documents.content: Trivium - Go Live Checklist, Scope Review, Reflection & Backlog Google Folder Link Go Live Checklist: Pre Go-Live: Aloware Integration Settings Complete Aloware Compliance Approval Aloware Campaign Registration Aloware user and number set up Aloware Line Registration Deliver Scope Review & Objective Overview Recordings Agree To Adoption Campaign Competition Set Go-live date Initial Team Training - Monday 10/28 1:30-2:30 Sales Team Onboarding & Overview Audit Team Onboarding & Overview Agenda - Make sure the following is all completed for each team member within Trivium; Calendar connection is complete Email sync is complete Hubspot chrome plugin is set up Phone number is connected Download Aloware Mobile app (Login) Individual Booking links are created Overview of New System Set Expectations For Go Live Review Adoption Campaign Create list of all places booking links are hosted and live within spreadsheet Deliver SM list of all individual booking links the sales team created following SOP video Clean Up Users & Seats (Tons of people who are in Hubspot that have not logged in for months or have never actually set themselves up) Go-Live: Wednesday 10/30 - 7:00 PM EST Trivium: Swap all booking links to HS booking links Sales Momentum: Turn on all workflows Turn off all irrelevant workflows Post Go-live: Mastery Training & Adoption Campaign Launch - Thursday 10/31 11:45 - 12:30 EST 1 week check in with leadership team scheduled Schedule project close & Backlog analysis → Overview Videos ← Intro Video - Watch First Part 1 - (Setter Process, app scoring, delegation process, priority system, front end structure) Part 2 - (Main Sales Pipeline, Audit Pipeline, Big Brain Workflows) Part 3 - (Contact/deal card views, deal tags, notifications, aloware, Dashboards & Reporting) Scope Review & Delivery: Timeline Outline: Timeline Duration: 60 Days Kick Off Date - August 29th Current Active Days - 53/60 Scope Outline: Application Scoring and Lead Delegation Build out a setter engine that enables application scoring and lead/meeting delegation. Optimize lead-to-booking percentages by routing leads effectively. Outbound Setter Engine: Leverage Sales Momentum's lead and priority list architecture. Ensure setters engage with the hottest leads quickly, focusing on speed-to-lead for both new and re-engaged leads. Rebook and Show Rate Process: Implement a rebook and show rate process that provides a simple, trackable workflow for setters. Enhance and track rebook percentages of no-shows. Include a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for confirming appointments within HubSpot. Outstanding Items: Appointment Confirmation Process SOP MOS Pipeline Management Engine: Implement the MOS pipeline management engine with conditional stage property mapping for both setters and closers. Simplify the sales process with well-defined deal stages and stage gates to maximize data collection and minimize time, effort, and friction for the sales department. Real-Time Dashboards: Create real-time dashboards for setters, closers, and sales leadership. Equip leadership with the data necessary to make strategic decisions and reduce manual data input, thus improving sales accuracy and efficiency. Outstanding Items: Finalize Audit Team Dashboard Finalize Sales Team Dashboard HubSpot Meetings Tool Implementation: Implement and optimize the HubSpot meetings tool with systemized lead delegation to enhance calendar efficiency and streamline meeting scheduling. Outstanding Items: Finalize Adding the right team members to booking links (Disco & Strat) Finalize Meeting rotation groups and weights (Disco & Strat) Systemized Handoffs Between Teams: Optimize handoffs between setters and closers, setters and auditors, and auditors and closers. Leverage HubSpot forms, integrated pipelines with association rules, and Setter/Closer Playbooks to ensure smooth transitions between these roles. Outstanding Items: CSP FINALIZATION (Need Trivium Input) Finalize Booking Link Playbook (Need to add individual booking links and other random links that might be needed by sales team) Finalize Disco Playbook Finalize Strat Playbook Environment Cleanup and Streamlining: Simplify and streamline all sales processes into one sales pipeline and one sales operations pipeline (auditor pipeline). Leverage deal types to differentiate product or client types within these pipelines. Clean up old workflows, properties, pipelines, stages, and reports. Reformat and standardize naming conventions and architecture across relevant objects,workflows, assets, and properties. Clean up and ensure proper integration of other software to maintain accurate data porting across the tech stack. Teams Setup: Build out business units and teams within HubSpot to reflect the roles assigned to relevant records. Incorporate "owner" properties to enhance team member-specific reporting in each key function. Reflection: Over Promised on timeline and under delivered In the initial onboarding prior to actually getting under the hood of the system I promised a 20-30 day turn around instead of 60 and fell short massively. I haven't taken on a project in a while and didn't not anticipate the clean up efforts and how busy I got post taking the project. LOTS of clean up was done A lot of much needed clean up was completed and we were able to get a majority of the system back to a cleaner set up - There is still some work to be done in order to finalize the clean up efforts; such as migrating pipeline / deal records, deleting workflows, properties, and lists. Very clear on Trivium's process and the new structure will be maintainable and scalable for the near and long term future. There are massive areas of opportunity to continue optimizing the system moving forward which I will list out at the bottom of this document. Trivium team needs to regain confidence and assign a “Key holder” to hubspot moving forward OR hire a Hubspot admin. As we approach the end of the this initial project the trivium team still needs to adopt and gain confidence in system adherence and administration. This will be the key to a successful revamp of the system and give the ability for SM to work on higher impact initiatives for the future opportunities. Potential for massive revenue and profit margin on marketing jump Trivium has massive opportunities across the sales process to make things more streamlined for management and sales team members. With the sound foundation we are moving into - you will run into code reds and some issues as things get turned on and adopted, however this is a clean foundation that marketing can be better plugged into and with future initiatives you will be able to accomplish what you have always wanted to - Turning chaotic systems into one of your companies biggest strengths AS LONG as you can stay organized and get curious about mastering Hubspot. Initial project pricing $15,000 This project in comparison to others would likely be a 25-30k project scope. We GOT A LOT DONE and worked on many things that were outside of scope but needed to be done. Internal Reflection Scores: Quality of work 8/10 Speed of implementation 6/10 Effort on project 7/10 Scope Full Completion Within Timeframe 6/10 Effectiveness Post Go Live Estimation 8.5/10 SM Internal Reflection Score: 7.1 Future Areas of opportunity to scope: Marketing UTM attribution, campaign structure, and reporting Campaign grouping UTM and source, medium, content direct attribution Marketing reporting and dashboards Lead Status & Lifecycle Stage Restructure and completion Upsell and renewal process for CSM Upsell and renewal pipeline Big brain workflow Reports and dashboards List segmentation For Email Marketing and Retargeting Charge Over Integration Line item structure and Sku Structure Charge Over Integration Set up Deal and contact association CEO Master Metrics Dashboard Email and SMS automation for lead and deal nurture Suggested Order Of Attack: Marketing UTM attribution, campaign structure, and reporti

documents.content: Trivium Data Clean Up Sign up for Ops Hub - Pro Link to quote to be provided (Estimated cost monthly $350-$450) Complete De-duplication Contacts Companies Complete Data Clean Up First Name / Last name Phone Number Formatting Email formatting Complete Property Clean up Duplicates Never used props. Workflow Error clean up Complete clean up across all WF errors Turn Off and Delete “Spring Cleaning” HS Clean Up Delete all not in use workflows Delete all not in use Forms Delete all not in use Lists Delete all not in use Reports ** Adjust all contact and deal property groups to Triviums Liking** Re-confirm Connection of Entry Points Entry Point Clean Up Applications Audit Forms Opt Ins Booking Links Double check for Hubspot tracking codes on all funnels and websites Migrate Data within pipelines to new pipelines Migration All Historical Sales Pipelines must be moved into the new “Main Sales Pipeline” One at a time. All automations must be turned off during the migration process so the close dates and time stamps do not adjust old deals to new revenue, etc… —----------- Trivium Tasks Move all active forms into Hubspot Folder “Active Entry Points” Alert Aaron once complete Create All Booking Links Required - Using Discovery And Strategy Event Types Under “Mina Elias” Alert Aaron for review once complete Integrate Chargeover with Hubspot Associ8 Pricing Page Lead Status & Lifecycle Stage (Typical Set Up) —-------------- Create the following Lead statuses: Lead Status is a more specific classification used primarily by sales teams to track the status of individual leads. It's focused on the process and activities that move a lead towards a sale. Compared to the property “Lifecycle Stage” this is much more specific as to where the prospect is within the sales process and is updated more frequently by the activity of the sales team. Our statuses include: New: A new lead that hasn't been contacted yet. Trigger: Any lead that has been created but has not been contacted by the assigned sales rep. Open: A lead that's being worked on but hasn't been qualified. Trigger: Any lead that has been assigned to a rep and has received sales activity (Calls) but has not responded to any communications or answered any phone calls. No Progress: A lead that has been contacted by the sales team over 25 times with no response, connection or communication made. Typically anyone in this lead status will be delegated back to marketing efforts or removed from all focus. Trigger: Contacted via phone call over 25 times with no response or connection made. In Progress: An active lead where contact has been established. Trigger: Any lead that has responded to an email, text, connected with a sales rep through a phone call, or books a “Discovery Call” meeting and triggers the event type. Unqualified: A lead that doesn't fit the target criteria of your program, product, or services. Trigger: This stage can be automatically triggered based on applications or by meeting a deal stage “Unqualified”. This can also be manually updated by the setters during the outbound process. Qualified: A lead that makes it into the end of your sales process and has been qualified during the discovery phase. Trigger: This stage is triggered when a prospect books a sales conversation with a closer and meetings the event type “Closing call OR Strategy Call” Closed Won: A lead that has become a customer. Trigger: When the deal stage “Won” is met. Closed Lost: A lead that's been concluded, either through conversion or because it was unqualified. Trigger: When a deal stage “Lost” is met. Bad Data: A lead that has fake or the wrong information for name, email or phone number. Trigger: This property is manually updated by a sales representative OR automatically if an email receives a “Bounced” OR “Undeliverable” status. Do Not Contact: A lead that is rude, problematic or requests to not be contacted again. Trigger: This stage is manually updated by a sales representative during conversations or if a lead requests to be added to the “DNC” list. This can also be triggered by the lifecycle stage “Declass” being met. Lead Status provides the sales team with a more granular view of where a specific lead is in the sales process, while Lifecycle Stage offers a broader view of where the lead fits within the overall customer journey. Create the following Lifecycle Stages: The Lifecycle Stage represents the various stages a contact or company goes through in the marketing and sales funnels. These stages help marketers and sales professionals understand where a lead is in the buying process. These stages are differentiated from the property “Lead Status” as these are high level and less in depth. Our stages include: Subscriber: Someone who has subscribed to a blog or newsletter. Trigger: Gives info to join a free community OR someone that has joined a news letter, podcast list, etc… Usually these contacts are around gaining value from the organization and are not yet far enough along to be contacted by sales. Marketing Qualified Lead (MQL): Someone who has shown more interest and has shared more information like an email address, phone number etc… This status is used most commonly for “Opt Ins” from a funnel, webinar, or downloadable asset. Trigger: Gives information through a form (Suggested info: First name, Last name, email, & Phone number. Sales Qualified Lead (SQL): A lead that the sales team has begun contacting and has entered into a discovery conversation with typically a setter inside of the sales department. Trigger: Booking a meeting or has a conversation over the phone with the event type “Discovery Call”. Opportunity: A contact who is associated with a deal that has a closer assigned. This is for all deals that make it past the discovery process and into one of the closer hands/conversations. Trigger: Booking a meeting that has an event type of “Closing / Strategy Call”. Any deals in or past the stage “Closing call booked” Customer: Someone who has made a purchase and has paid for a program, product, or service. Trigger: Completes an invoice or meets the “Deal Won” Stage Evangelist: A satisfied customer who is promoting the product or brand. This could be someone who has given a testimonial, delivered qualified referrals OR is in multiple programs. Trigger: Has multiple deals won with more than one product, service or program. This is also triggered manually by someone who has delivered a testimonial or referrals. Declass: A customer or client that has received a refund, completed a chargeback, or that is extremely problematic. Trigger: Deal stage refund or chargeback has been met. This can also be manually updated by the fulfillment or client success team for clients that cause many problems and issues inside of the program, community, etc. Bad Lead: A contact that is marked as bad data or do not contact

To set this up in the way that works best for you, we just need to know: Do you already use Slack? If so, we can integrate everything into your existing workspace through Slack Connect. If not, we'll send you a simple invitation to join your private channel with us. Just reply with your preference and the email address you'd like us to use, and we'll handle the rest. documents.name: SLA for internal communications.docx
documents.content: Service Level Agreement for Internal Communications “This Service Level Agreement ("SLA") sets forth the terms and conditions under which the internal communications will be effective within the organization.” Service Description All the team members will provide the following services to other departments within the organization: Be active and responsive during company business hours (4 hours overlap for non-US members - 6a-10a PST) Acknowledge the messages they receive from their coworkers and set the expectations for a response. Before scheduling a meeting team members have to make sure to check their peer’s calendar for open time-slots. Manage their slack statuses according to what they are doing. (brain- for deepwork, food- for dinner/ lunch etc) Service Availability The team will be available during normal business hours, Monday through Friday, but managing their time flexibly making sure they overlap with 6 AM - 10 AM PST which will be exclusively reserved for communications and Meetings with US Staff. Deep work will need to be completed prior or after these times. Team members need to set their normal business hours in Google Calendar. (check with your manager if you do not know how to set this up) Response Time The team has no more than 2 business hours to respond to any request via slack/ email/ Monday.com (during business hours). If they cannot provide a full answer they need to acknowledge the message and set the expectations accordingly. Requests received outside of normal business hours will be addressed on the next business day. Non-compliance Team members are expected to follow-up with their requests 2 times before escalating a non-compliant member to their respective manager. Team members that were flagged more than 3 times will receive a final written warning for non-compliance. Review and Revisions This SLA will be reviewed quarterly to ensure that it remains relevant and effective. Revisions may be made as necessary to reflect changes in business requirements. By signing below, all team members within the organization agree to the terms and conditions of this Service Level Agreement.

The current system requires enhancements to streamline workflows, Doc ID: 5d62ee5cdeffaf91ccfe36318cca8cd8af595677 improve data accuracy, and boost overall efficiency. The primary objectives of this project are to build and optimize several key components within HubSpot, clean up the existing environment, and ensure seamless handoffs between different teams and processes. The overall objective is to have these processes run efficiently by team members while being able to have real-time dashboards and leaderboards to make data driven decisions as quickly as possible. The specific objectives include: �. Setter Engine for Application Scoring and Lead Delegation: Build out a setter engine that enables application scoring and lead/meeting delegation. Optimize lead-to-booking percentages by routing leads effectively. �. Outbound Setter Engine: Leverage Sales Momentum's lead scoring algorithms and priority list architecture. Ensure setters engage with the hottest leads quickly, focusing on speed-to-lead for both new and re-engaged leads. �. Rebook and Show Rate Engine: Implement a rebook and show rate engine that provides a simple, trackable workflow for setters. Enhance and track rebook percentages of no-shows using the MOS pre-call sequence to maximize show rates. Include a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for confirming appointments within HubSpot. �. MOS Pipeline Management Engine: Implement the MOS pipeline management engine with conditional stage property mapping for both setters and closers. Simplify the sales process with well-defined deal stages and stage gates to maximize data collection and minimize time, effort, and friction for the sales department. �. Real-Time Dashboards: Create real-time dashboards for setters, closers, and sales leadership. Equip leadership with the data necessary to make strategic decisions and reduce manual data input, thus improving sales accuracy and efficiency. �. HubSpot Meetings Tool Implementation: Implement and optimize the HubSpot meetings tool with systemized lead delegation to enhance calendar efficiency and streamline meeting scheduling. �. Systemized Handoffs Between Teams: Optimize handoffs between setters and closers, setters and auditors, and auditors and closers. Leverage HubSpot forms, integrated pipelines with association rules, and Setter/Closer Playbooks to ensure smooth transitions between these roles. �. Environment Cleanup and Streamlining: Simplify and streamline all sales processes into one sales pipeline and one sales operations pipeline (auditor pipeline). Leverage deal types to differentiate product or client types within these pipelines. Clean up old workflows, properties, pipelines, stages, and reports. Reformat and standardize naming conventions and architecture across relevant objects, workflows, assets, and properties. Clean up and ensure proper integration of other software to maintain accurate data porting across the tech stack. �. Customer Communication and Dialer Software Implementation: Retain and/or adjust customer communication via email and text at key stages of the sales process. Doc ID: 5d62ee5cdeffaf91ccfe36318cca8cd8af595677 Implement dialer software to enhance setter efficiency and improve communication workflows for setters. ��. Business Units and Teams Setup: Build out business units and teams within HubSpot to reflect the roles assigned to relevant records. Incorporate "owner" properties to enhance team member-specific reporting in each key function. Implementation Phases and Timeline: Phase 1: "MOS" Sales Build Duration: 30 days Deliverables: Build and configure the setter engine, outbound setter engine, rebook and show rate engine, MOS pipeline management engine, real-time dashboards, HubSpot meetings tool, and dialer software. Clean up and streamline the HubSpot environment. Phase 2: "MOS" Sales Training and Optimization Duration: 30 days Deliverables: Train the team on the new systems and processes. Provide live virtual training sessions, documentation, and SOPs. Optimize systems based on initial feedback and usage. Resources: Implementation Type: Remote (on-site support available for an additional fee) Key Team Members: Mina Elias, Daniel LeBlanc, and potential other team members. Client Responsibilities: Attend scheduled meetings on time. Provide necessary access to current systems. Designate an internal project manager. Pricing and Payment Terms: Total Project Cost: $15,000 per Aaron Platt Support and Maintenance: Ongoing Support: Managed service at $6,000 per quarter or $22,000 per year if paid upfront. Additional Services: Available upon request. Timeline: Start Date: To be discussed on call Project Duration: 2 months, broken down into the two phases outlined above. Critical Deadlines: Limited project spots are available. Once spots are filled, the next availability could be several weeks to months later. documents.name: The Trivium Playbook + DSP.docx
documents.content: Overview The Playbook functions as your primary reference, offering clear guidance and navigation to the exact Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) you require. Whether it's a detailed process description or a specific task protocol, the Playbook streamlines access to vital SOPs, ensuring efficient and consistent operations. If you can't find an SOP you believe should be included, we welcome your input. Please reach out to the Operations Team for assistance. Table of Contents General Notion Notion is the software Trivium uses for creating and managing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Here’s the SOP on How to: Login to Notion using Shared Access. Google Workspace Applications Drive Google Drive is a cloud-based file storage and synchronization service. It allows our team to organize files, documents, and folders efficiently. Department Shared Drives A shared drive is an organizational structure within Google Drive that lives parallel to My Drive. Shared drives support files owned by an organization rather than an individual user. Our agency utilizes department-specific shared drives to centralize and manage team resources efficiently. Access restriction measures are implemented to guarantee the privacy and security of data. Reach out to your Supervisor and/or Manager for access to your department’s shared drives. Access/Sharing Sharing files and folders is crucial for collaboration. This section will explain how to control access to documents, both internally and externally. It covers the process of setting file permissions, sharing files via links, and utilizing shared drives for streamlined collaboration. Calendar Creating an Event (Meeting) Accept/Decline It is of utmost importance to effectively handle meeting invitations and your availability. Please make sure to either accept or decline all calendar invites promptly. When you join your respective teams, you will be included in certain events at both the company and team levels. It is crucial that you review your calendar daily and accept or decline these events based on your availability. Teammate’s Calendar Understanding a teammate's schedule is essential for collaborative work. This video will show you how to view and interact with a teammate's calendar, ensuring easy coordination and scheduling of meetings or tasks. Trivium - Employees and Clients Calendar This is a comprehensive and centralized calendar which serves as a vital resource for keeping our team organized and well-informed, and ensuring that we maintain an organized and efficient work environment. This video will show you how to add this to your calendar. Calendar ID: c_ope85o1gd9tkmhauhr38r1j2do@group.calendar.google.com It includes several key events and dates, such as: Approved PTOs: This calendar displays all approved Paid Time Off (PTO) requests submitted by our employees. It allows us to track who is on leave, when, and for how long, ensuring seamless workflow planning and coverage. Employee Birthdays: Employee birthdays are a special part of our workplace culture. The calendar features the birthdates of our team members, so we can celebrate and show appreciation on their special days. National Holidays: National holidays are essential days off for our employees. This calendar marks these dates to help everyone plan around these public holidays. Client Start Dates: For our clients and projects, we include the start dates in this calendar. This information is vital for our project management and client communication, ensuring a smooth and well-coordinated kickoff for every client engagement. Meetings (Internal) Internal Meetings are meant to be an effective place for team members to use their problem-solving skills and critical thinking skills to solve any ongoing challenges. These meetings are meant to make us proactive in solving any issues client accounts or departments are facing. Team members should be ready to prepare potential solutions to overcome these obstacles. ALL team members are encouraged to share their perspectives. Call Recording Recording all calls is optional but is highly recommended, whether they are internal client calls, external client calls, or departmental calls. You may choose to record the Zoom call to your computer or to the cloud. Cameras Numerous advantages come with keeping your camera on during meetings! Encourages interpersonal connections among participants It's quite straightforward: there's value in having a virtual face-to-face conversation with the individuals you're meeting with. While many of us may wish for in-person collaboration with our colleagues in a traditional office setting, utilizing tools like Google Meet is the next best option. As humans, we have an inherent need to connect with one another. Leaving your camera on signals your interest, engagement, and attentiveness during the call. Conversely, having your camera off in virtual meetings often indicates a sense of disconnection. Sparks active involvement and engagement Seeing every team member makes it easier to engage them, solicit their input, or field questions. Maintaining your camera can also help you stay focused on meeting objectives, particularly if you tend to multitask. Conveys non-verbal cues Gestures like nodding and smiling play a significant role in gauging your team's sentiments about an upcoming project. According to Forbes, many influential leaders acknowledge that non-verbal cues, including body language, constitute 55% of all communication. Humans rely on body language to establish connections with one another. Building trust among peers requires them to feel comfortable around you. Leaving your camera on allows your personality to shine through, enabling you to leverage non-verbal cues to your advantage. Feel free to leave your camera off if: You're not feeling well There are days when working effectively means staying in your pajamas on the couch, and that's perfectly acceptable! You're in a distracting environment We've all experienced chaotic days. If your home workspace presents a backdrop of dirty dishes, children's toys, and laundry, it's advisable to keep your camera off. Balancing the need to appear professional, share your home environment with your team, and maintain a tidy background can be challenging. Nevertheless, resist the temptation to keep your home entirely devoid of the presence of children, pets, or partners—your team values seeing the real you! Virtual Meeting Etiquette Mute Yourself Remember to keep yourself muted unless you are actively speaking. Regardless of whether you're in a home or office setting, unexpected occurrences can draw attention to your square for the wrong reasons. We strive to maintain efficient meeting flow, so kindly remain on mute unless you wish to contribute, are prompted with a question, or the floor is open for discussion. This practice will also help minimize background noise during the call. Hands Up When you have a question during a Zoom meeting, make use of the hand-raise feature! Located at the bottom of your screen, you'll find an icon representing a raised hand, which will alert the host. Employ this feature judiciously! The raised hand will be clearly visible on the video frame of the participant who initiates it. It's easy to spot, but please ensure a smooth transition to your question, and if you're already speaking, wrap up your point before asking. Control The Meeting Strive to avoid speaking over other people especially your clients, yet maintain control of the call using our meeting agenda! This is a simple principle. Always keep in mind to be courteous, while also valuing your time and establishing clear expectations regarding the allotted duration for the call from the outset. Presenting Share the specific window you are actively using! Limiting your screen sharing to a single window is essential to prevent any Slack notifications or other pop-up notifications from appearing in the bottom right corner, where they could be visible to cl

We have set up this dedicated Slack channel for us to centralize all comms here: day-to-day activities, questions, updates... Everything! This will help us collaborate effectively, making sure nothing is missed and we keep working in the same direction. @Alina Sheludiak will be your dedicated Client Success Manager, your main point of contact, and the person who owns Creatives Optimization. She’ll be sharing the next steps to guide you through the process shortly! We have also attached here to this message your [quote/agreement], just to keep it handy and everyone aligned. Thank you and welcome on board! —--------------- Hi @client Welcome to Trivium! We're excited to kick off this partnership. My name is [Your Name], and I’m the Operations Associate and Slack Channel Manager. I’m here to support you as we get started and help make great things happen together. As part of the process, our Fulfillment Team will be added to this Slack channel once payment has been received or on the official start date of the service whichever comes first. (include this if client is in nyp or ww) Looking forward to working with you! Or this message for existing client This is your Slack channel, where you can communicate for all your needs. The trivium team is also here in case you need any help. INTRODUCE THE TEAM - Send this once paid Here is a list of the Trivium Team members in the channel: @Mina Elias - CEO of Trivium Group @Maureen Mc Loughlin - Chief Operations Officer @Manuel - Onboarding Manager @Alina Sheludiak - Client Success Manager @Oleksandr Burkat - Amazon Brand Support Specialist @Robin - Amazon Graphic Designer @Hannah Tampioc - Listing Image Strategist @Marina Wahib - Finance Manager @Jazz @ Victoria - Operations Admin ATTACH THE SCOPE OF SERVICES and PIN TO CHANNEL Send ONB form Kindly complete the form below to help us gain a deeper understanding of your brand and create a design that authentically captures its essence: Fill in the listing creation form https://forms.clickup.com/9014250980/f/8cmn3f4-37054/98PWWGOBV33IAINDFB Fill in the creatives creation form https://forms.clickup.com/9014250980/f/8cmn3f4-28734/LTKTSJ2OI8LPTGZT79 Fill in the SEO creation form https://forms.clickup.com/9014250980/f/8cmn3f4-78434/RB82RIK3B3RRHE28FI For any questions or further assistance, feel free to reach out to our Graphic Design team. x Messages for the Client Reachout over Email first Hi [NAME], I hope you are doing well. Thank you for signing the agreement! We’re excited to get started and deliver value to your business. To get started, please accept the invite to our Slack channel by following this link: [Hyperlink to Slack Channel Invite] Once you’ve accepted the invite, you’ll have direct access to our dedicated channel, where we can communicate next steps, share documents, and coordinate seamlessly. Please let us know if you have any questions or concerns. Best regards, Follow up by email if they didn’t join Slack Hi [NAME], Just a quick follow-up to my earlier message — I wanted to make sure you saw the invite to our dedicated Slack channel [Hyperlink Slack Invite Link]. Joining this channel is the next key step in kicking off your onboarding. It’s where we’ll: Share next steps and helpful resources Introduce you to your dedicated Team Coordinate everything related to your partnership with Trivium Once you're in, we’ll get the ball rolling and make sure everything is set up for success. If you have any questions or need help accessing Slack, I’m happy to assist. Looking forward to seeing you there! Best, Once added on Slack Hi @client, Welcome to Trivium — we’re so excited to have you onboard! I’m [NAME], your [ROLE], and I’ll be your main point of contact throughout the onboarding process. My role is to ensure everything runs smoothly and that you feel fully supported as we get started. Over the next few days, we’ll guide you through a few simple steps to get everything set up. One of the first steps will be confirming your preferred billing method so we can finalize your account on our end. We offer two secure, pull-based payment options for your monthly subscription: ACH or Credit Card. documents.name: 11_Trivium - Go Live Checklist & Scope Review.docx
documents.content: Trivium - Go Live Checklist, Scope Review, Reflection & Backlog Google Folder Link Go Live Checklist: Pre Go-Live: Aloware Integration Settings Complete Aloware Compliance Approval Aloware Campaign Registration Aloware user and number set up Aloware Line Registration Deliver Scope Review & Objective Overview Recordings Agree To Adoption Campaign Competition Set Go-live date Initial Team Training - Monday 10/28 1:30-2:30 Sales Team Onboarding & Overview Audit Team Onboarding & Overview Agenda - Make sure the following is all completed for each team member within Trivium; Calendar connection is complete Email sync is complete Hubspot chrome plugin is set up Phone number is connected Download Aloware Mobile app (Login) Individual Booking links are created Overview of New System Set Expectations For Go Live Review Adoption Campaign Create list of all places booking links are hosted and live within spreadsheet Deliver SM list of all individual booking links the sales team created following SOP video Clean Up Users & Seats (Tons of people who are in Hubspot that have not logged in for months or have never actually set themselves up) Go-Live: Wednesday 10/30 - 7:00 PM EST Trivium: Swap all booking links to HS booking links Sales Momentum: Turn on all workflows Turn off all irrelevant workflows Post Go-live: Mastery Training & Adoption Campaign Launch - Thursday 10/31 11:45 - 12:30 EST 1 week check in with leadership team scheduled Schedule project close & Backlog analysis → Overview Videos ← Intro Video - Watch First Part 1 - (Setter Process, app scoring, delegation process, priority system, front end structure) Part 2 - (Main Sales Pipeline, Audit Pipeline, Big Brain Workflows) Part 3 - (Contact/deal card views, deal tags, notifications, aloware, Dashboards & Reporting) Scope Review & Delivery: Timeline Outline: Timeline Duration: 60 Days Kick Off Date - August 29th Current Active Days - 53/60 Scope Outline: Application Scoring and Lead Delegation Build out a setter engine that enables application scoring and lead/meeting delegation. Optimize lead-to-booking percentages by routing leads effectively. Outbound Setter Engine: Leverage Sales Momentum's lead and priority list architecture. Ensure setters engage with the hottest leads quickly, focusing on speed-to-lead for both new and re-engaged leads. Rebook and Show Rate Process: Implement a rebook and show rate process that provides a simple, trackable workflow for setters. Enhance and track rebook percentages of no-shows. Include a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for confirming appointments within HubSpot. Outstanding Items: Appointment Confirmation Process SOP MOS Pipeline Management Engine: Implement the MOS pipeline management engine with conditional stage property mapping for both setters and closers. Simplify the sales process with well-defined deal stages and stage gates to maximize data collection and minimize time, effort, and friction for the sales department. Real-Time Dashboards: Create real-time dashboards for setters, closers, and sales leadership. Equip leadership with the data necessary to make strategic decisions and reduce manual data input, thus improving sales accuracy and efficiency. Outstanding Items: Finalize Audit Team Dashboard Finalize Sales Team Dashboard HubSpot Meetings Tool Implementation: Implement and optimize the HubSpot meetings tool with systemized lead delegation to enhance calendar efficiency and streamline meeting scheduling. Outstanding Items: Finalize Adding the right team members to booking links (Disco & Strat) Finalize Meeting rotation groups and weights (Disco & Strat) Systemized Handoffs Between Teams: Optimize handoffs between setters and closers, setters and auditors, and auditors and closers. Leverage HubSpot forms, integrated pipelines with association rules, and Setter/Closer Playbooks to ensure smooth transitions between these roles. Outstanding Items: CSP FINALIZATION (Need Trivium Input) Finalize Booking Link Playbook (Need to add individual booking links and other random links that might be needed by sales team) Finalize Disco Playbook Finalize Strat Playbook Environment Cleanup and Streamlining: Simplify and streamline all sales processes into one sales pipeline and one sales operations pipeline (auditor pipeline). Leverage deal types to differentiate product or client types within these pipelines. Clean up old workflows, properties, pipelines, stages, and reports. Reformat and standardize naming conventions and architecture across relevant objects,workflows, assets, and properties. Clean up and ensure proper integration of other software to maintain accurate data porting across the tech stack. Teams Setup: Build out business units and teams within HubSpot to reflect the roles assigned to relevant records. Incorporate "owner" properties to enhance team member-specific reporting in each key function. Reflection: Over Promised on timeline and under delivered In the initial onboarding prior to actually getting under the hood of the system I promised a 20-30 day turn around instead of 60 and fell short massively. I haven't taken on a project in a while and didn't not anticipate the clean up efforts and how busy I got post taking the project. LOTS of clean up was done A lot of much needed clean up was completed and we were able to get a majority of the system back to a cleaner set up - There is still some work to be done in order to finalize the clean up efforts; such as migrating pipeline / deal records, deleting workflows, properties, and lists. Very clear on Trivium's process and the new structure will be maintainable and scalable for the near and long term future. There are massive areas of opportunity to continue optimizing the system moving forward which I will list out at the bottom of this document. Trivium team needs to regain confidence and assign a “Key holder” to hubspot moving forward OR hire a Hubspot admin. As we approach the end of the this initial project the trivium team still needs to adopt and gain confidence in system adherence and administration. This will be the key to a successful revamp of the system and give the ability for SM to work on higher impact initiatives for the future opportunities. Potential for massive revenue and profit margin on marketing jump Trivium has massive opportunities across the sales process to make things more streamlined for management and sales team members. With the sound foundation we are moving into - you will run into code reds and some issues as things get turned on and adopted, however this is a clean foundation that marketing can be better plugged into and with future initiatives you will be able to accomplish what you have always wanted to - Turning chaotic systems into one of your companies biggest strengths AS LONG as you can stay organized and get curious about mastering Hubspot. Initial project pricing $15,000 This project in comparison to others would likely be a 25-30k project scope. We GOT A LOT DONE and worked on many things that were outside of scope but needed to be done. Internal Reflection Scores: Quality of work 8/10 Speed of implementation 6/10 Effort on project 7/10 Scope Full Completion Within Timeframe 6/10 Effectiveness Post Go Live Estimation 8.5/10 SM Internal Reflection Score: 7.1 Future Areas of opportunity to scope: Marketing UTM attribution, campaign structure, and reporting Campaign grouping UTM and source, medium, content direct attribution Marketing reporting and dashboards Lead Status & Lifecycle Stage Restructure and completion Upsell and renewal process for CSM Upsell and renewal pipeline Big brain workflow Reports and dashboards List segmentation For Email Marketing and Retargeting Charge Over Integration Line item structure and Sku Structure Charge Over Integration Set up Deal and contact association CEO Master Metrics Dashboard Email and SMS automation for lead and deal nurture Suggested Order Of Attack: Marketing UTM attribution, campaign structure, and reporti

documents.content: Managing Event-Related Leads Gather & upload the list to HubSpot Done with real event. Recording and SOP to be done for future cases – already requested. Maureen to confirm with Mina if Brandy and her team should be managing the contact import and list creation. Process Steps Trivium should host the landing page to support the ads strategy. Marketing will give visibility of events on sales-marketing channel and when we are going to receive a list. A week in advance is required to prep: Setters availability. Welcome email with proper call to action. Setters start outbound activities as soon as we receive the list. Priority: warm or contacted in the last 90 days. We are contacting all attendees that: Are not our clients. Haven’t churned in the past 3 months. Are not competitors. The closers are not in active communication. Change from cold to warm based on the general criteria. Warm lead: someone who fills out an audit form, books a call, or is introduced to us directly via email or SMS Cold lead: someone who downloads a lead magnet, signs up for webinar, attends an event, etc. Now there is another category that’s truly cold: which is when we do cold outbound but since we aren’t doing that - we can ignore that for now Until when are we contacting? We reach out to the leads on multiple channels for upto 2 weeks until we leave them to unresponsive and allow the marketing emails to start nurturing them. Email marketing starts 2 weeks after we received the list. Brandy will exclude the list we create in HubSpot from our general Email Marketing Campaign. Email marketing strategy will be the same general strategy followed for the rest of contacts. Brandy to work with a contractor to incorporate adds into this. Brandy Lyman to add details about how this will be done. Brandy Lymanto add more marketing strategies to take if relevant.

documents.name: Reviews Sales Call Script v1.docx
documents.content: Reviews Sales Script. Aug 30, 2024 Purpose of this document Provide the Head of Reviews some guidelines to manage Sales Call, especially when the Sales team does not participate. Call Structure Build Rapport Hey is this [CLIENT NAME]? Hey - It’s [your name] - How is your day going so far? Awesome - [share something about your day] Remind me, what part of the world are you calling in from? Oh cool! I am from [your location] Great well - I know we got a limited amount of time here so… are you ready to jump in? Set the agenda So what I’ve found that work best on these calls is first diving deeper into the specifics of your current situation, the business, your goals, to understand how that’s working right now, and ultimately what you feel are the specific challenges that are keeping you from growing. Now… Once we get some clarity there - if we can help, then I’m more than happy to walk you through our Reviews process and what would that look like. Cool? Sound Good? I understand you are dealing with [challenge], is that right? Can you tell me a little bit more about that? Current Situation I would love to know more about where your business is at now. As I understand… [present what you have learned about the brand and product] Product Category / Niche. Is it a difficult (e.g. alcohol)? Is it a product that usually works very well to get Reviews? Amazon Reviews status (rating, # orders, # reviews). Instagram status (# followers & posts). Is my understanding correct? Is there anything else about your current status that I have not mentioned, and you consider relevant? [Take notes, correct your understand if necessary and move on to the Desired State] Desired State I would like to learn more about your biggest needs and challenges you are currently facing in regards with your reviews. Is there anything that is not working in your business right now and would need immediate attention from our Reviews team? So far, what have you tried to fix this in the past, if anything? How long have you been trying to fix XYZ? Have you reached out to anyone else to get help with this in the past? Are you working with anyone now? Have you been out there considering other companies to possibly work with? What has been the biggest challenge that has kept you from meeting the results you are expecting? Before finding us, have you been out there looking for anything else that would give you what you are wanting here? What do you want to achieve? What are your short, mid and long term plans? Find out what we need to do now to gain their trust, and what’s the long term vision we need to keep in mind as their partner? Great! I have a much deeper understanding of what you are looking for. I would like to ask you a few more questions to have a better knowledge of your buyers, your product and your competition too. Target customer characteristics: Who is buying your product? Mention anything relevant: age, gender, country, interests, status, profession, clues/commonalities, other characteristics. Where do your customers hang out? The success of this strategy is very much dependant on how well we target your customer. Where they may hang out? What pages do they follow? What are they interested in? Who do they follow? When customers start noticing the effects of your product? Is there an optimal time for review requesting. How much time after receiving the product is the best to ask the review after? Who are your main competitors? What makes your product stand out from the competition? Okay, [NAME], let me recap to make sure I’m clear on your goals and the results you are expecting… “Get your rating from X status to X new status within X period of time”... or “Get X number of reviews within X period of time”. Pitch Look I don’t feel like I have any more questions… Is there anything else that you feel like we haven’t covered that I need to know? Well [Name] - based on what you told me previously, we can definitely help… I would love to walk you through what we can offer you, how does it sound? [Walk them through the sales deck] If the financial proposal is an issue, gather more details: For a second, let’s just pretend that money is out of the equation. How do you feel about the process specifically? Do you feel like ultimately, it’s what you need to get to [goals they want to achieve]? Gotcha, no problem… So just for clarity here… what’s important to us is ALIGNMENT ...because this isn’t like a course or something where we just give you a bunch of videos and modules and tell you “good luck”. If you come in and do this, we’re rolling up the sleeves and getting in the trenches WITH YOU. We’re fighting this fight with you. So if we’re going to put our reputation on the line and dedicate not only our resources but our teams time to your success, I want to make sure that money and logistics aside you are BOUGHT IN to the process and you feel like it’s the most effective route to [their goal]. So, it sounds like your more in a “HOW” can I do this place to where you’re 100% certain this is the shortest and most effective route to ([their goal], it’s just a matter of making it work financially, right? If their interest is truly there, let the lead know you will check with our Management team if there are other budget options that could work for them, based on their needs. This would be the main next step. Otherwise, present next steps following the deck. Closing When you reach the end of the Sales Deck, clear up questions, check client’s temperature and agree on next steps.

documents.name: Copy of CRM Report.xlsx
documents.content: Please create a copy of the sheet and edit. TIA GET STARTED WITH YOUR CRM REPORT If you are looking for a system to organize your contacts, solidify a sales process, and automate some of your ongoing tasks then you need a CRM (customer relationship management) solution. This template provides you with the basics of a CRM. It's the perfect place to start if you aren't quite ready for a full-blown CRM with advanced features. This mini-CRM automatically saves changes so you will never lose data. To get started, just enter your contacts manually or copy and paste existing data into this sheet. How to use this template 1.0 | When setting up this mini-CRM for the first time, go to the "Settings" tab to define categories for characteristics such as Contact Type for People or Stage for Opportunities | 2.0 | Keep the CRM up-to-date by updating or adding rows as you engage with "People", "Companies", and "Opportunities" | 3.0 | Use the CRM to plan your daily, weekly, and monthly goals. The "Dashboard" provides a summary of how your sales pipeline is doing to help you decide what to address next. Let's walk you through the tabs listed at the bottom of this sheet. Dashboard Think of the Dashboard tab as your control panel for your opportunities. You'll see the following information: - The total value of all your opportunities - Total number of People, Companies, and Opportunities in this CRM - The number of Opportunities by stage and the value of Opportunities by stage This is a great place to start planning your daily goals! People A Person is someone you have already qualified to do business with. They may be a current customer, potential customer, or some other type of contact or relationship. This is the Person that works for a Company you want to do business with. Companies A Company is an organizational entity that you are either doing business with now, or may be doing business with soon. We like to think of the Company as the building that the People you are dealing with work in. The Company record is the top level record that we relate other records such as People or Opportunities to. Opportunities An Opportunity represents any kind of business development effort that you would like to track and move along through a process. You could also call an Opportunity a "deal" or a "sale". An Opportunity could represent the sale of a product, billings associated with services, or an activity that has no direct monetary value, like increasing your press coverage. Setting This is where you define the following items that will set the data rules in your Sheet: - Contact Type for People and Company - Stage, Status, Source, and Loss Reason for Opportunities You'll want to adjust this to what makes the most sense for your business process. documents.name: AdLabs SOP.docx
documents.content: 🛠️ Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Managing Clients & Users in AdLabs Objective: This SOP outlines the step-by-step process to connect a client to AdLabs, add internal users to manage the account, and remove clients or users when needed, ensuring smooth onboarding, access control, and data hygiene. Management aspects: The following rules need to be followed while deciding to add or not a client in AdLabs: We will manage 5 or more parent ASINs for this client. The client is spending >=$10k/month on ads. The strategist wants this client to be added to AdLabs. For ex., even if a client has >=5 parent ASINs and is spending >=$10k/month on ads, but the strategist doesn't need the client added, we will not add it. The main internal report where we monitor the added and removed clients from AdLabs is this:https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1WpzrLGU3rmAcDZXqVecuLHBfhDFR3ZNy/edit?gid=356838649#gid=356838649 (It can be found in the Canva of the adlabs-trivium Slack channel.) Each time we need to add or remove a client from AdLabs, the main responsible person for AdLabs needs to update this file by adding a new record or changing the status of a client and the date it was added/removed. Weekly actions: Each week we should check AdLabs to see if the added clients comply with the rules based on which they were added to AdLabs, and if not, remove the client from the software in order to preserve Trivium’s expenses. At the end of the third week of each month, it is necessary to fill out the budget request (https://forms.clickup.com/9014250980/f/8cmn3f4-40234/0PMIEHQMNXQAVPIHN8) to ask for the amount we expect we'll be paying AdLabs for in the following month (existing eligible clients + expected new clients). ✅ 1. How to Connect a Client to AdLabs 📌 Purpose: Allow AdLabs to access a client’s Amazon Ads account to monitor and manage campaigns. 🔄 Process: Step 1: Log in to AdLabs Go to AdLabs Platform Log in using your admin/agency credentials. The new user that we want to add, can log-in in AdLabs before or after we add him/her to the platform. Step 2: Create a “Team” Before adding a client to AdLabs, we need to create a “team.” Considering that at Trivium, we access clients’ Seller Centrals from multiple analytics accounts, for each analytics account, a team was created, and based on which analytics’ email we access the client in Seller Central, from the same “team,” we access the same client here in AdLabs. Important mention: In AdLabs, the name of clients is the same as in Seller Central. There are particular cases when the name is not the same even with the SC, and this is because AdLabs is pulling data from Amazon’s API where, even if the name was changed, the first initial name that the client set is stored. It is told that this will be fixed in the future. Navigate to the left-hand menu → Click on “Manage Teams”. Step 3: Click “Create New Team” Type the team’s name and click “Create Team” Step 4: Add a new client We can click on the team’s name or Navigate to the left-hand menu → Click on “Manage Profiles”. We can navigate between teams in the Manage Teams menu or in the top right corner to choose which team to work on. Once we picked the necessary team, we then click “Manage Profile” button in order to choose which client to ad to AdLabs from the ones we have access from this email in SC. Step 5: Client Connects Account Once we found the client, we want to add to AdLabs we toggle from not active to active the status from the column “Manage in AdLabs” and Click “Confirm” button at the bottom. ✅ Confirm: Once added, the client should be reflected in the list of “Profiles” There is a need of a few hours for the data to upload and to be able to work on client’s ads. 👥 2. How to Connect a User to Work on the Client’s Ads 📌 Purpose: Assign PPC specialists or team members to specific client accounts within AdLabs. 🔄 Process: Step 1: Go to “Manage Teams” Tab Step 2: Click Members” Important note: to add new users is, so far, possible only from Mina’s “owner” credentials. Step 3: Click “+ Add New Member” Type the work email of the new users and click “Add member”. ✅ Confirm: Once added, the new user will appear in the Member’s lists. If it’s necessary to add a user to all teams. For all of them it will be necessary to repeat the process. ❌ 3. How to Remove a Client or a User 📌 A. Removing a Client Step 1: Go to “Manage Profiles” section of AdLabs and click on “Manage Profiles” button. Step 2: Find the Client and untoggled it’s “Manage in AdLabs” status from active to paused. Step 3: Click “Confirm”. Confirm that you want to remove access. This will disconnect AdLabs from their Amazon Ads account and delete all synced data. ⚠️ Important: Once removed, historical data will no longer be accessible. Export any reports before deletion if needed. 📌 B. Removing a User Step 1: Go to “Manage Teams” section of AdLabs. Navigate to the Members tab. Step 2: Search for the User Use the email or name to locate the user. Step 3: Click “the bin icon” in order to remove the user from that specific team. User will immediately lose access and be logged out if active. If it’s necessary to remove a user from all teams, it will be necessary to repeat the above process for all of them. 📋 Best Practices Always export important performance data before removing any client. Review access monthly to ensure only active team members are assigned. When offboarding a client, confirm with leadership before disconnecting. Resolving Marketplace Access Issues in AdLabs Situation: When trying to add a profile to a team in AdLabs (e.g., Peachly AU to the "analytics+7@triviumco.com" team), you might face a situation where the US marketplace is not appearing, even though access to the US market is available in Seller Central. This issue can occur when the Amazon Ads API does not correctly update the advertising account name for the US marketplace, especially if the advertiser's account name has recently been changed. Problem: BrandID mismatch: The advertising account name update reflects correctly for marketplaces such as CA and MX but not for the US marketplace. Marketplace visibility issue: When attempting to select the US marketplace in AdLabs, it may not show, even if access is granted through Seller Central. Solution: If you encounter this issue, follow these steps to resolve it: Identify the BrandID: In AdLabs, look for the BrandID associated with the CA or MX profile. The BrandID should still be visible and associated with the correct marketplace in AdLabs, even if the US marketplace is not displaying. Search for the BrandID in the US Profile: Open the AdLabs platform. Use your browser's Find function (Ctrl + F or Cmd + F) to search for the same BrandID. This should help you locate the US account associated with the same BrandID, even if it's not showing up in the initial marketplace selection dropdown. Assign the Profile: Once the correct US BrandID is found, assign it to the team (e.g., "analytics+7@triviumco.com"). Ensure that this profile is now linked to the US market in your AdLabs system. Precaution: Monitor for Future Issues: If you encounter this problem frequently, it could be due to changes in the advertiser's account name. Make a note of the BrandID and regularly verify that it is linked to all desired marketplaces. Notify Developers: If this issue continues or new ones arise, reach out to the AdLabs development team for further investigation.

MANAGED SERVICES AGREEMENT This Managed Services Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into and becomes effective on October 29, 2024(“Effective Date”) between Sales Momentum, LLC (“Sales Momentum”), a Delaware limited liability company, with principal offices located in Hollywood Florida, and Trivium Group(“Client”). Sales Momentum and Client, collectively, are sometimes herein referred to jointly as “Parties”, and individually, as “Party”. RECITATIONS WHEREAS, Sales Momentum has extensive expertise, systems, software, integrations, education, skill, training, process, business connections, and Doc ID: 6d2046dbdfb8898c3386e3515ff66ca578de57f6 experience in sales, marketing, and client success to businesses and offers these various services to businesses in several industries; WHEREAS, Sales Momentum and Client are already engaged in a business relationship through a mutually executed Engine Services Agreement; WHEREAS, Client is desirous of engaging in a continuous business relationship with Sales Momentum for it to manage on a monthly basis the engines purchased in their Engine Services Agreement. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing and the mutual agreements and covenants set forth here, the parties agree as follows: Sales Momentum has agreed to provide the Managed Services as contemplated in this Agreement, Client has agreed to compensate Sales Momentum for such Managed Services, and the Parties have agreed to do so in accordance with the terms and conditions in this Agreement. �. SERVICES 1.1 Managed Services. Client shall have access to and receive the following: �. Ongoing Maintenance: Sales Momentum shall keep your systems running at commercial performance with regular maintenance. �. Data Integrity: Sales Momentum will manage duplicates and data. �. Onboarding/Offboarding New Team Members: Sales Momentum will handle the onboarding and offboarding of new employees �. Quick Edits/Fixes: Sales Momentum shall promptly address any issues to minimize downtime. �. Light User Training: Sales Momentum shall equip your team with the knowledge they need to utilize Hubspot effectively. �. Support and Guidance: Sales Momentum will provide continuous assistance. �. Monthly Meetings: Client shall have access to a monthly 30-minute performance review with a Sales Momentum Manager Doc ID: 6d2046dbdfb8898c3386e3515ff66ca578de57f6 �. Slack Connect: Sales Momentum will provide a channel for communication with Client during the Term of this Agreement. Each of these services is collectively referred to as the “Managed Services”. At all times material hereto, Sales Momentum shall provide, the Managed Services only as commercially reasonably possible. 2. PAYMENT 2.1 Monthly Service Fee. In consideration of Sales Momentum’s performance of the Managed Services, You shall pay Sales Momentum a monthly service fee for the Elected Services in the amount referenced in the above section labeled Services & Payment Terms, which shall be due and payable in equal payments on or before the first (1st) day of each month and on or before the third (3rd) day of each month during the Term (the “Service Fee”). The first Service Fee payment shall be due on the Effective Date and will apply to the time period from the Effective Date until the last day of the Effective Date’s month, which such time period will not be prorated. In the event that Sales Momentum performs any additional services not included in the Managed Services, the parties will negotiate in good faith such additional compensation as may be appropriate to compensate Sales Momentum for such additional services. 2.2 Payment Disputes. Sales Momentum reserves the exclusive right to consider any and all refunds, full or partial, of the Service Fee. If the Client has questions about this Agreement, it should submit its comments to the relevant Sales Momentum consultant. Client agrees not to request, advise, file a claim, or seek Client’s bank or credit card company for a chargeback for consideration paid under this Agreement. (“Chargeback”). Client agrees to waive any rights Client may have under applicable state and federal truth in lending laws or otherwise (including, but not limited to, under Client’s credit card issuer’s procedures for resolving such disputes). Client agrees that any disputes that Client may have with respect to the Purchase Price paid hereunder must be addressed directly between Client and Sales Momentum. If a Chargeback occurs, Client shall have materially breached this Agreement and shall forfeit all remaining Managed Services that have not yet been performed under the Agreement. Company shall have no further obligation to Client. Further, the amount of the Chargeback shall be subject to a finance charge of 1.5% per month on any outstanding balance, or the maximum permitted by law, whichever is lower. You will pay all amounts due hereunder in US Dollars by credit card, check, ACH wire, or other electronic transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated in writing by us. All amounts payable to us under the Agreement will be paid by you in full without setoff or withholding for any reason. Further, Sales Momentum shall be entitled to Doc ID: 6d2046dbdfb8898c3386e3515ff66ca578de57f6 recover from Client all damages, reasonable and necessary attorneys’ fees, and costs associated with pursuing collection and/or recovery of the amount of the Chargeback. 3. TERM AND TERMINATION 3.1 Term. The Term of this Agreement shall start on the effective date until the first day of the following month, but will then automatically renew on that day and will then automatically and continuously renew on the first day of every month thereafter, whereby you will be charged the applicable Service Fee set forth in Section 2.1, until either Party terminates this Agreement in accordance with Section 4.2. Each and all monthly term renewal months will be governed by the same terms and conditions of this Agreement. 3.2 Termination. The Managed Services renewal will be continuous until otherwise decided by either Parties written notice provided thirty (30) days before the termination date in accordance with Section 5.6. If the Managed Services Option is terminated by You, You will owe the full amount of the Service Fee for the current month of termination. 3.3 Suspension of Services. Sales Momentum may, directly or indirectly and by any lawful means suspend the Managed Services without incurring any resulting obligation or liability, if: (i) Client fails to pay any amount when due under the Agreement; (ii) Sales Momentum believes, in its sole and absolute discretion, that Client or any of its representatives have failed to comply with any term of the Agreement, including the Cooperation provision described in paragraph 6.3 of the Audit Agreement; (iii) the Term is terminated or expires; or (iv) Sales Momentum receives a judicial or other governmental demand or order, subpoena, or law enforcement request that expressly or by reasonable implication requires it to do so. documents.content: Agreement is updated by sales person to include the following Notes for finance Include any notes on rev share Include any notes on first month billing Include any notes on different start dates of different services Notes for fulfillment Include notes on specific ASINs to focus on Include notes on any budget preferences Include notes on any agreed upon strategy Include notes on other services to be discussed Include notes on important things to be handled by fulfillment first Agreement get sent to client Agreement gets signed by our team Agreement gets signed by client Automation should let us know an agreement is signed Sales ops team checks pandadoc daily to make sure that any agreement signed has been notified to the ops and finance team Signed agreement (not paid) should trigger the ops and the finance team Ops team: Ops team should send an email to the new client giving them a summary of next steps and making sure they get in slack Ops team should also notify client to pay, as well as notify sales team to follow up with client to pay Ops team follows up daily with client if they are not in slack, emailing them asking them to get in slack Ops team only confirms client is in slack once they respond in slack Ops team follows up daily with client and sales team to make sure client pays Ops team to notify fulfillment team that client has not paid yet so no work is to start at all Ops team pulls the AI summary of the sales call and adds it to Hubspot, as well as the client Canvas Ops team creates the Canvas for the client and fills out the template Ideally there is an automation that pushes a signed agreement to the master database and creates a new row highlighted which notifies finance and rest of team to fill it out NOTE: We need a task to be created in ClickUp for new client onboarding that is a Kanban so we know the status of each client Finance team: Finance team talks to sales team and reads agreement and makes sure they understand billing cycle and nuances Finance team adds client to our billing platform and sets up subscription If any invoices or subscriptions are set up for the future, finance team creates an automated reminder 5 days before the payment to confirm that the invoice will be valid still and timeline did not change Finance lets the fulfillment team know that billing is successful and the team can begin working on the client Finance updates the client database with all the relevant information ---------------------------------------------------------- Canvas template: Brand Name: Seller Central Name: Seller Central Email Login: Start date: ASINs: Product Links Brand Table Brand Goals Keyword Tracker Billing Issues and Requests Brand Assets Analytics - My Real Profit External Links Brand Website Instagram Facebook Client Points of Contact Trivium Team Main POCs Client Success Manager: PPC Strategist: Support Roles: Secondary Services CSM: Analyst: Operations associate: Finance Manager: Leadership Team CEO: Director of Operations: Sales call summary: ---------------------------------------------------------- Once the client has signed, paid and been confirmed they are added in Slack, an onboarding call needs to be initiated The CSM will send a message to the client letting them know on 2 calls they need to schedule The first call is the onboarding call Message: Hey CLIENT, I’m going to send you a booking link to book the onboarding call. This needs to be done ideally ASAP. We will not talk about any strategy there, I will just let you know what onboarding is going to look like and make sure we have everything we need from you to hit the ground running NOTE: We should make this part of the onboarding email the ops team sends and have the CSM prepared for this On the onboarding call, the CSM discusses the following What are the next steps of onboarding The team gets into your seller central account and confirms they have all the permissions they need Our analytics software is connected to your account and we make sure the data is flowing in accurately You fill out the brand table so we have a rough idea of your goals and can see profit accurately in our software (skip what you don’t know) We will book a strategy call once the team has had a chance to deep dive in the account. On that call we cover strategy, eliminating waste, finalizing budgets and what improvements needs to be done. You also tell us your exact goals and preferences and communication style. How do you like to be communicated with? Do you want daily updates? How do you want to see your weekly updates? Can you handle multiple of our team members or want 1 only? Do you like to be extra granular or just want us to explain what happened with a plan? Are you comfortable with Slack? Do you understand the Canvas? Do you have a time preference for calls? Do you have any non Amazon questions? Are you ready to give us access, go over the brand table and fill it, and connect the software with the correct permissions? Lets schedule our next strategy call 72 hours from now – and we will discuss an exact plan of action for your account. Is there anything specific you want us to cover in the plan of action? The CSM should document anything worth noting about the client and all their answers in the Canvas The CSM should then schedule a meeting to debrief the internal team and PPC team The PPC team should then work on a client strategy as follows and add screenshots in a presentation Identify all wasted adspend – STR and targeting tab Identify high performing low budget campaigns Identify low ACOS keywords not being targeted Identify account level budget caps Identify portfolio level budget caps Identify if there is any software in the background working Identify low organic ranking on relevant keywords with good search volume Show the MRP results for each product highlighting spend, sales, CTR, CVR, TACOS, Profit and refunds Propose maintaining budgets for 2 weeks while doing some recomposition Identify low SEO products starting from highest to lowest revenue generators Comment on the listing quality and CVR and CTR if it is an issue Comment on product price point if it is higher than the range in the market Answer all questions the client had from the onboarding call Note down the strategy for each product (scale or optimize and the budget) The CSM should then prepare for the call with the client The CSM has the call with the client Call structure as follows Call agenda Go over our findings Go over what we think strategy should be Answer your questions See if you want to adjust strategy Write down action items We go and execute Present the deck that was made Ask if client has questions Ask if client wants to adjust strategy or budget Write down action items in the Canvas with dates After that – every day the strategist should be sending an update on the action items The CSM should then schedule a follow up call to check on how things are going ideally in 1-2 weeks Message: Hey CLIENT, lets schedule a quick call to see how you are feeling so far with progress and make sure we are aligned Call agenda should be Check on results so far – show how sales and profits changed since we started How do you feel about the current strategy and onboarding? How do you feel about the team? What can be better? How do you feel about the communication and updates? Are they too much? Is there anything specific you want us to update you on? Do you have any questions? Can we talk about a couple of things that could help? Creatives can be better – we have a team Reviews can be better – we have a team Lets summarize action items and notes of this call All action items and notes are added to Canvas From then on – there should be a more regular meeting cadence The goal is to discuss updates, make sure strategy is good, align on things to move forward, and discuss what can be done to grow the brand (reference Mina video)
