documents.content: Assignment Questions SECTION 1 1.Explain what is PPC and how it works?(2 marks)2 PPC, or pay-per-click, is an online advertising model where advertisers pay a fee each time one of their ads is clicked by a user. It's essentially a way for sellers to "buy" visits to their product listings or websites, rather than earning those visits organically. In the context of Amazon, advertisers create ads for their products and bid on specific keywords or phrases. When a user searches for that keyword, the ads with the highest bids and quality scores are displayed in prominent positions on the search results page. The advertiser is only charged when their ad is actually clicked, so they're paying for potential customers to visit their product pages. 2.What are the two main goals of PPC? (2 marks)1.5 a) Increase product visibility: PPC helps advertisers boost their products' exposure in the Amazon marketplace, allowing them to reach a wider audience. By placing their ads on search result pages or product detail pages, sellers can increase the likelihood of their products being seen by potential customers, leading to more sales. b) Generate sales and revenue: The ultimate goal of PPC is to drive sales and increase revenue for the advertiser. When executed effectively, PPC can help sellers achieve a higher return on investment (ROI) by targeting the right keywords and creating compelling ads that encourage users to click and ultimately make a purchase. Improve organic rank SECTION 2 1. How do you tell the difference between a paid (PPC) product ad and an organic product ad? (1 mark)1 The primary difference between a paid (PPC) product ad and an organic product ad lies in their placement and labeling. Paid product ads are labeled as "Sponsored" or "Ad" on the search results page, product detail pages, or other designated areas, indicating that the advertiser has paid for the ad's placement. Organic product ads, on the other hand, appear in the search results based on Amazon's algorithm without any additional payment and do not carry any "Sponsored" or "Ad" label. 2. Explain the three different types of sponsored ads and mention where they displayed on Amazon pages? (3 marks)3 Sponsored Products These ads promote individual products and appear in the search results or on product detail pages. They blend in with organic listings but are marked as "Sponsored." Sponsored Brands These ads help promote a brand and its product portfolio. They typically appear at the top of the search results page and consist of a headline, logo, and up to three products. The ad is labeled as "Sponsored" and directs users to a customized landing page or the brand's store. Sponsored Display These ads target specific audiences or product categories and can appear on product detail pages, search results pages, or even off-Amazon sites. They are visually similar to display ads and are labeled as "Sponsored" as well. 3. Do we always want to rank on the top of page one? Explain (2 marks)2 Ranking at the top of page one may not always be the primary goal, as it can lead to higher costs and choice overload for consumers. Striking a balance between visibility and cost-effectiveness is crucial. Depending on the product and competition, a position in the top three or the middle of the first page can still ensure visibility, convey trustworthiness, and enable easier price comparison, ultimately driving sales and maintaining a healthy return on investment. Understanding consumer psychology helps sellers optimize their ad placements on Amazon for more effective advertising strategies. 4. Which ad type is the most important? (1 mark)1 There isn't a universally "most important" ad type as the significance of each ad type depends on the advertiser's goals and strategies. Sponsored Products are often considered the most crucial ad type for many sellers, as they directly promote individual products and seamlessly integrate with organic listings. However, Sponsored Brands can be vital for brand awareness and promoting a range of products, while Sponsored Display ads can help with retargeting or reaching specific audience segments. The optimal ad type(s) will vary based on the seller's objectives and target audience. SECTION 3 1. Explain why we only use 1 ad group per campaign (2 marks)2 We use only 1 ad group per campaign to ensure better control over keywords and targeting, allowing for easier optimisation and analysis of ad performance. 2. What is the campaign naming convention? How do we structure campaign names? (2 marks)2 The campaign naming convention is a structured format that includes the Product Identifier, Ad Type, Match Type, Purpose, and Source. This format makes campaigns easily identifiable and manageable. 3. Explain the three different campaign bidding strategies? Which one do we use by default? (3 marks)1.5 The three campaign bidding strategies are dynamic bids (down only), dynamic bids (up and down), and fixed bids. By default, dynamic bids (down only) are used, as they automatically adjust bids to optimise for conversions. Also need the explanation. Down only - Amazon will reduce bids when less likely to convert, Up and Down - Amazon will increase or decrease bid based on likelihood of conversion, fixed bids - remain fixed 4. Explain each of the four auto campaign targeting types? (4 marks)1 The four auto campaign targeting types are close match, loose match, substitutes, and complements. These targeting types help Amazon automatically match ads to relevant search terms and products. Needed explanation for each Close match - Amazon shows ad for closely related search terms Loose match - Amazon shows ads for loosely related search terms Complements - shows on product pages for complementary products Substitutes - shows on product pages for similar products 5. Why do we separate auto targeting types into separate campaigns? (1 mark)1 Separating auto targeting types into separate campaigns allows for better control, tracking, and optimisation of ad performance. 6. What is the difference between broad, phrase and exact keyword campaigns? (3 marks)2 Broad, phrase, and exact keyword campaigns differ in their specificity. Broad match targets any search term containing the keyword, phrase match targets search terms with the exact keyword phrase, and exact match targets search terms identical to the keyword. Phrase - exact keyword phrase with words added at the beginning or the end 7. Which campaigns are used for keyword discovery? (2 marks)1.5 Auto campaigns and broad match campaigns are primarily used for keyword discovery, as they target a wider range of search terms.also phrase 8. Where will a product targeting ad appear? (1 marks)1 A product targeting ad will appear on product detail pages or in the search results, targeting specific products or product categories. 9. Explain the refine feature in the category targeting campaign.( 2marks)2 The refine feature in category targeting campaigns allows advertisers to narrow down their target audience by applying filters such as brand, price, or star rating. 10. Where can you source product targets to add to a product targeting campaign? (4 marks)4 Product targets can be sourced from Amazon's suggested targets, competitors' product pages, or by analysing the performance of auto campaigns. 11. How do we identify products that are targeting us (1 mark)1 To identify products that are targeting us, we can monitor the "Sponsored Products Related to This Item" section on our product detail pages and track competitors' ads. 12. What are brand protection campaigns? Why do we use them? (2 marks)2 Brand protection campaigns are designed to protect our brand by bidding on our brand name and branded keywords. They prevent competitors from dominating the search results for our brand terms. 13. Why do we use big bids for brand protection campaigns? Sponsored Products The most popular type of sponsored ads. Ad products are displayed on the search page and product page. They look like organically displaying products. 2. Sponsored Brands More customized type of sponsored ads. Ad products are displayed on the search page. They can be shown with a video or a picture and lead users to the product page, amazon landing page, or store. 3. Sponsored Display Can be displayed in various places such as sides, top or bottom of the search page, and product page. Ad products can be shown with customized pictures. 3. Do we always want to rank on the top of page one? Explain (2 marks)2 No. Sometimes it is more efficient to lower the bid and stay in the middle of the search page, for example. Buyers like to scroll the page and explore different options before making a final decision. So if you place your ad in the middle or at the bottom of the first page, it may bring as many sales as the top of the search and cost less. 4. Which ad type is the most important? (2 marks)2 Campaign naming convention is a clear and systematic way of naming ad campaigns. Naming structure: unique code for each product - ad type - match type - campaign purpose - source of targeted keywords/products - number of the campaign as each campaign contains up to 5 keywords 3. Explain the three different campaign bidding strategies? Which one do we use by default? (3 marks)3 1. down only - Amazon lowers the bids in real time when the ad is less likely to convert a sale. It helps us to spend less. 2. up and down - Amazon raises the bids up to 100% in real time when the ad is more likely to convert a sale, and lowers the bids when the ad is less likely to convert a sale. It can be used for a new launch. 3. fixed bids - Amazon uses exactly the same bid you adjust. Default bid strategy - down only 4. Explain each of the four auto campaign targeting types? (4 marks)4 Close match - Amazon analyses product listing and shows the ad to the customers who use search terms closely related to your product Loose match - Amazon analyses product listing and shows the ad to the customers who use search terms loosely related to your product Substitutes - Amazon shows the ad to the customers who view listing pages of your main competitors Complements - Amazon shows the ad to the customers who view listing pages of products that complement yours 5. Why do we separate auto targeting types into separate campaigns? (1 mark)1 It allows you to monitor and optimise each targeting type. If you put several types in one campaign, they may show different results and you cannot control daily spend on each of them. 6. What is the difference between broad, phrase and exact keyword campaigns? (3 marks)2.5 Exact - search term is exact same as a targeting keyword Phrase - search term can vary but the order of words is the same as in a targeting keyword Broad - search term differ from the targeting keyword, this match type is very loose 7. Which campaigns are used for keyword discovery? (2 marks)2 Auto campaigns Phrase campaigns Broad campaigns 8. Where will a product targeting ad appear? (1 marks)0.5 On competitors' listing pages 9. Explain the refine feature in the category targeting campaign.( 2marks)2 You can refine product targeting in subcategory by price range, reviews star ratings and brand names. While refining targeting, you can see how many targeted products you get. It helps to make your campaign efficient without unprofitable targeting. It also helps you to find performing patterns and use them. 10. Where can you source product targets to add to a product targeting campaign? (4 marks)4 1. Extract data from auto campaign search terms reports, segregate performance and volume 2. Use amazon suggestions when create campaign 3. Find competitors that are targeting us and use them. Pay attention to reviews 4. Find complementary products in adjacent categories using yasiv.com 5. Find competitors by analyzing Amazon search page. You can use Helium10 Xray or Black Box 11. How do we identify products that are targeting us (1 mark)1 Go to your product page and look at Sponsored Products Related to This Item, there you’ll find competitors that target us. 12. What are brand protection campaigns? Why do we use them? (2 marks)2 They are campaigns that targets keywords with our brand name or our other products. For these campaigns, we collect keywords with all possible variations of the brand name or company name. For brand protection strategy, we create 17 campaigns in SP SB SD of all match types. Buyers search our products using our brand name and these searches are the most profitable to us. Besides, even if the competitor pays more for the keyword with your brand, you will be shown first as the most relevant. 13. Why do we use big bids for brand protection campaigns? (2 marks)2 This type of targeting is the most relevant to us and the most profitable. So we must win competitors to be displayed and to get our sales. This is why we need to use high bids for brand protection campaigns. 14. What is ‘purchases remarketing’ in sponsored display campaigns? (1 mark)1 It is a type of advertising where you can target shoppers who purchased from you in the past, purchased similar products or products within the same category. SECTION 4 1.What is the goal of Helium 10 research (2 marks)2 To determine the keywords to run PPC for and to rank for. This research also helps to learn more about shoppers behaviour. 2. documents.content: Assignment Questions SECTION 1 1.Explain what is PPC and how it works?(2 marks)2 PPC stands for pay-per-click which means that every time a user clicks on an ad, advertisers pay. In PPC campaigns, advertisers bid on specific keywords in order to achieve a higher rank. The person that bids the most will be shown on the top of the page. 2.What are the two main goals of PPC? (2 marks)2 The two main goals of PPC are: - Driving traffic into our listings as cheap as possible; - Ranking organically by generating conversions; It's important to spend the least amount of money and bring the most amount of people, not overspending on keywords. SECTION 2 1. How do you tell the difference between a paid (PPC) product ad and an organic product ad? (1 mark)1 A paid PPC product has the grey label " sponsored" on the top of the product title. Also, I've noticed that paid PPC products appear on the top or the bottom of the page, but organic product ads are usually in the main body of a page. 2. Explain the three different types of sponsored ads and mention where they displayed on Amazon pages? (3 marks)3 There are 3 types of sponsored ads: 1. Sponsored Products ads look incredibly organic and appear in search results and on the bottom of the product page. They have the label "sponsored" near the product title. 2. Sponsored Brands appear at the top of the search results page. 3. Sponsored Display ads appear on product detail pages, customer review pages and at the end of the page. 3. Do we always want to rank on the top of page one? Explain (2 marks)2 Not necessarily. We have to take into account the buyer psychology. For example, if there are too many options available, customers will tend to scroll a lot until they understand all products' specifics. Also, when a product is unique and other competitors have lower-quality products, it is likely that the most distinctive product will be bought. 4. Which ad type is the most important? (1 mark)1 All of them are important, but in our case, the most effective are Sponsored Products Ads, as our goal is to drive sales of a specific product. SECTION 3 1. Explain why we only use 1 ad group per campaign (2 marks)2 The reason is that we need to have more control over our bids and budgets. If there are multiple ad groups, we won't know the amount of money that goes to each group and how the budget was split. Also, it is easier to track the performance and make adjustments. 2. What is the campaign naming convention? How do we structure campaign names? (2 marks)2 The campaign naming convention is the way someone structures the names of his advertising campaigns. It's important to be able to analyze data easier so the naming has to be done as clear as possible. PPC it's all about pattern recognition. Firstly, you need to create a product code for all products, like an abbreviation. An example of the campaign name structure is: Product identifier - Ad type - Match type - Purpose - Source. 3. Explain the three different campaign bidding strategies? Which one do we use by default? (3 marks)3 1. Dynamic Bids - Down Only: Amazon will lower your bid in real-time when your ad is less likely to convert to a sale. As Mina says, this strategy is more conservative and helps to avoid wasteful clicks. This is the strategy he suggests using, 2. Dynamic Bids - Up and Down: Amazon will raise your bid by up to 100% in real-time when your ad may be more likely to convert to a sale, and lower your bid if it is less likely to convert to a sale. 3. Fixed Bids: Amazon will use the exact bid and any manual adjustments you set. 4. Explain each of the four auto campaign targeting types? (4 marks)4 There are 4 auto campaign targeting types: 1. Close Match: The ads will be displayed for search keywords closely related to your products. This targeting type is great for identifying relevant keywords for the campaign. 2. Loose Match: The ads will be displayed for search keywords less closely related to your products. 3. Substitutes: Ads will be displayed for products that are similar to your products (direct competitors). 4.Complements: Ads will be displayed for products frequently purchased or used together (complementary to your products). 5. Why do we separate auto targeting types into separate campaigns? (1 mark)1 We use only one targeting type per campaign because it allows us to allocate more budget to the best-performing targeting type, and avoid wasting budget on targeting types that are not performing as well. 6. What is the difference between broad, phrase and exact keyword campaigns? (3 marks)3 Broad: Ads will be shown for any search query that is related to the keywords you've selected, including plurals, misspellings, synonyms, and related phrases. 2. Phrase: Ads will be displayed for search keywords that include the exact phrase you've selected, and any additional words before or after the phrase. 3. Exact: Ads will only appear if the search query exactly matches the selected keywords, with no additional words. 7. Which campaigns are used for keyword discovery? (2 marks)1 Broad campaigns. 8. Where will a product targeting ad appear? (1 marks)1 A product targeting ad will appear at the bottom of the product detail page, in the "Sponsored products related to this item" section, below the product information and above the customer reviews. 9. Explain the refine feature in the category targeting campaign.( 2marks)1 The refine feature in the category targeting campaigns allows you to narrow down the targeting of your ads to more specific subcategories that are most relevant to your products. 10. Where can you source product targets to add to a product targeting campaign? (4 marks)3 We can check the "Sponsored products related to this item" section on our products page and find ASINs that may be relevant targets for our campaign. Also, we can source through Amazon search results and visit our competitor's product page. 11. How do we identify products that are targeting us (1 mark)1 Search our product on Amazon Visit the product detail page 3. Look through "Sponsored products related to this item" 12. What are brand protection campaigns? Why do we use them? (2 marks)1 Brand protection campaigns are launched to protect a brand and prevent other advertisers from using someone's brand name or trademarks to advertise their own products. These campaigns use targeted keywords and negative keywords to prevent a brand from appearing in irrelevant search results. We use them because we need to protect our clients' names in every possible situation. 13. Why do we use big bids for brand protection campaigns? (2 marks)2 We need to ensure that our products appear first in search results when customers search for our brand name or related keywords. We use high bids so that we can outbid other advertisers who may want to use our brand name for promoting their products. 14. What is ‘purchases remarketing’ in sponsored display campaigns? (1 mark)1 Purchase remarketing in sponsored display campaigns is the strategy where Amazon targets customers who have previously purchased products from your brand, a similar product, or a product in the same category. SECTION 4 1.What is the goal of Helium 10 research (2 marks)1.5 The goal of Helium 10 research is to help Amazon sellers in keyword research, listing optimization, and sales tracking. It allows sellers to identify profitable product niches, and analyze competitors in order to make decisions about their own products. 2. Explain in detail the steps for keyword research using Helium 10 (4 marks)4 Step 1: Determine the Main Keyword We need to find the most common and main keywords relevant to our product (seed keywords ). This can be done through competitor analysis. Enter selected keywords into Helium 10's keyword research tool (Magnet) and generate a list of related keywords, along with data regarding each keyword. documents.content: Assignment Questions SECTION 1 1.Explain what is PPC and how it works?(2 marks)2 PPC stands for Pay-Per-Click and it used to drive traffic in amazon. For every customer clicks the product, seller pays money for the advertisement. Basically, it let's the seller choose how much they are willing to spend to boost there product listing in amazon. It can be $2 or $3 depending on the customer. The more it shows on the listing, the more it will likely to be sold. 2.What are the two main goals of PPC? (2 marks)1 Goal is to how to spend the least amount of money and how getting the most out of our ads. To drive traffic to the lisitng as cheap as possible. SECTION 2 1. How do you tell the difference between a paid (PPC) product ad and an organic product ad? (1 mark)1 on amazon, you will be differentiate them by the "sponsored" title.Paid ads (PPc) has that title and an organic ad does not. It may look the same but the only difference would be the "sponsored" title. 2. Explain the three different types of sponsored ads and mention where they displayed on Amazon pages? (3 marks)3 The three types would be Sponsored Brand, Sponsored Display and Sponsored Products. Sponsored products has the "sponsored" title in the picture or description. For Sponsored Brand, it could be the headline or image to the profile of the seller. Sponsored displays can be seen randomly in the amazon space, it usually contains the product and the reviews of the product. 3. Do we always want to rank on the top of page one? Explain (2 marks)0 Yes. It is important to always be on the top of page one because customer usually tend to click on those and buy the product. Customer usually get hook to the first thing they see so it is important that the product we are doing ads to is in the top of the list. 4. Which ad type is the most important? (1 mark)1 Most important ad type would be the Sponsored Product. This focuses on a specific product you want to sell, not as a whole but the prodcut itself. SECTION 3 1. Explain why we only use 1 ad group per campaign (2 marks) To be specific and not entangled with other ad group. 1 2. What is the campaign naming convention? How do we structure campaign names? (2 marks)2 To name the campaign systematic way. To know what campaign it belongs in. The structure of campaign name would be Product indentifier - Ad Type - Match Type - Purpose - Source 3. Explain the three different campaign bidding strategies? Which one do we use by default? (3 marks)3 Dynamic bids - Down only, Dynamic Bids - up and down, and Fix bids. For Down only, it lower the bids if the system thinks that the bids will not turn into a sale. For Up and Down, it makes the bid higher when the system thinks it will most likely convert into a sale and lower the bid if it less likely to. For For bids, as the name suggest, it is a fix rate for the each click or bids. We use Dyanmic bids - Down only by default. To be conservative and to less likely spend more money on bids. 4. Explain each of the four auto campaign targeting types? (4 marks)3 Close Match, Loose Match, Subsititutes, and Complements. Close match and loose match are almost the same. It means that the ad will show to shoppers who closely search to the keywords. Subisititues are for direct competitors and Complements are for complementary products. 5. Why do we separate auto targeting types into separate campaigns? (1 mark)1 To see what type of auto targetting performs the best. If we put all 4 campaigns in one product, we are going to be stuck with auto targetting types that doesn't perform well. We want to spend more money on the targetting type that does well. 6. What is the difference between broad, phrase and exact keyword campaigns? (3 marks)1.5 For Broad keyword campaigns, It will show the ad to customers that has the keyword in it. Even it is not related, it will show. For Phrase keyword, if you do have 2 word keyword, the ad will be shown to the customer using those 2-word keyword even if it is jumbled. For Exact, the ad will only show to the customer who searches for the exact keyword. 7. Which campaigns are used for keyword discovery? (2 marks)1 Broad, Phrase and Exact 8. Where will a product targeting ad appear? (1 marks)0 It will be shown on the searched list on amazon. 9. Explain the refine feature in the category targeting campaign.( 2marks)2 You can include/exclude brands, adjust the max/min price of the product, adjust the star rating. 10. Where can you source product targets to add to a product targeting campaign? (4 marks)2 Amazon suggestion or Competitor product target 11. How do we identify products that are targeting us (1 mark)0.5 Check the "sponsored products related to this item" selection. 12. What are brand protection campaigns? Why do we use them? (2 marks)0.5 Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, and Sponsored Dsiplay. We use them to make an ad with the same brand or type of product within the seller. 13. Why do we use big bids for brand protection campaigns? (2 marks)0.5 To Highlight all of the other products that the seller is selling. 14. What is ‘purchases remarketing’ in sponsored display campaigns? (1 mark)1 The ad will show to the shoppers who bought the product to you in the past or bought the product in the same category. SECTION 4 1.What is the goal of Helium 10 research (2 marks)1.5 To search the most profitable keyword to use for advertising the product 2. Explain in detail the steps for keyword research using Helium 10 (4 marks)2.5 Magnet - Determine the main keyword relevant to your product. X-Ray - search for the top listing products using that keyword. Cerebro - narrow down keywords based on competitors ranking Keyword Tracker - Track organic rank of targeting keywords SECTION 5 1.If the budget is tight, which two auto campaigns do we initially launch?(2 marks)2 Close match and Substitute 2.What is the maximum number of keywords we use in a campaign? (1 mark)0 as many as you can think of within the budget range 3. What are branded keyword campaigns? (1 mark)0.5 It is a keyword that is for specific brand. High market brands. 4. How many days do we wait before optimizing new campaigns? (1 mark)1 7 days 5. What is upsell? and what type of campaign is used to upsell? (2 marks)2 Upsell is to advertise your own product. Product targeting campaign should be used to target the ASIN of each product. 6. If we have a low sponsored and organic rank do we increase or decrease bids and why? (2 marks)1 we can try to increase the bid to show the ad more frequently but the right keywords should be chosen. SECTION 6 1.Explain the terms sessions and unit session percentage (2 marks)2 Session is when a persion clicks on the same ad twice but only count it as one session because it is the same person, under the same amazon account. Unit session is calcuted as the units ordered divided by total number of sessions. 2.How do you calculate cost per session? (1 mark)1 PPC cost divided by the number of session 3.How do you calculate cost per conversion? (1 mark)1 cost per session multiply by the number of people needed to make a conversion 4.Explain the difference between ACOS and TACOS and how they are calculated (2 marks)2 ACOS is PPC Spend over PPC Sales. TACOS is PPC Spend over overall sales including organic. ACOS is not as accurate as TACOS due to amazon does not take into account the organic sales. 5.What is the most important metric? (1 mark)1 Profit. This number determines if you are making money. 6.What do we expect to happen to sessions and sales if the PPC spend goes up? (2 marks)2 we expect that session and sales would go up also 7.If we increased spend and noticed sessions went up but sales didn’t, what could be the reason and what metric do we look at to determine this? (2 marks)2 It might be because we targeted the wrong people to click on our product. Wrong choice of keywords. 8.What metrics do you expect to go up and what metrics do you expect to go down when scaling up in a bulking phase? (4 marks)1

documents.content: Assignment Questions SECTION 1 1.Explain what is PPC and how it works?(2 marks) Ans. PPC stands for Pay per click. this is a platform where you can introduce your product to many more people or customers through advertising. PPC is a performance-based advertising model where advertisers pay for ad clicks. It provides a flexible and measurable way to reach targeted audiences, drive traffic, and achieve marketing objectives by leveraging keyword targeting, bid management, and ad optimization techniques on digital advertising platforms. 2.What are the two main goals of PPC? (2 marks) Ans. 1. Driving Traffic - The client's product must be more profitable than expenses. 2. Generating Conversions - PPC Advertising must do the work to make that happen. SECTION 2 1. How do you tell the difference between a paid (PPC) product ad and an organic product ad? (1 mark) Ans. The difference between paid PPC Product Ad and Organic Product Ad is: paid PPC Product Ad is willing to invest a lot to get the first spot on the result page and is labeled Sponsored which means under PPC Advertising while Organic Product Ad does not have a Sponsored label but appears on the 1st page of the result page. 2. Explain the three different types of sponsored ads and mention where they displayed on Amazon pages? (3 marks) Ans. 1. Sponsored Products - are ads for individual product listings that appear within search results and on product detail pages. These ads are keyword-targeted, meaning sellers choose relevant keywords for their products. Sponsored Products appear in various locations on Amazon: ● Search results pages ● Product detail pages 2. Sponsored Brands - are ads that promote a brand and its product portfolio. These ads typically include a custom headline, logo, and a selection of products. Sponsored Brands appear highly in specific locations on Amazon: ● Search results pages ● At the bottom of search results pages ● On product detail pages 3. Sponsored Display Ads - are used to target customers both on and off Amazon. These ads can be shown to shoppers who have previously viewed your products or similar products, or actively searching or browsing on Amazon. Sponsored Display Ads are displayed in the following locations: ● On Amazon - on product detail pages, customer review pages, and below search results while ● Off Amazon - across various websites and apps within Amazon's advertising network 3. Do we always want to rank on the top of page one? Explain (2 marks) Ans. Ranking at the top of page one on Amazon search results can be highly desirable for many sellers and advertisers, but it may not always be the optimal strategy depending on various factors. Ranking at the top of page one can be advantageous for visibility and click-through rates, it's crucial to evaluate the overall impact on your business objectives, cost considerations, and conversion metrics. Consistent Monitoring and Optimization is also needed to maximize your success on Amazon. 4. Which ad type is the most important? (1 mark) Ans. Sponsored Products are likely the most important ad type because driving sales for specific products is priority and also 80% of the campaigns comes from this ad type. Determining the most important ad type on Amazon depends on your specific goals, product offering, and target audience. Each ad type serves a distinct purpose and can be valuable in different scenarios. SECTION 3 1. Explain why we only use 1 ad group per campaign (2 marks) Ans. This is why we structure each campaign with one ad group—to clearly identify and optimize the performance of specific targets and match types that generate orders and sales for a product. By focusing on better-performing targets, we can allocate our budget more effectively, investing in higher bids where they deliver superior results, and avoiding excessive spending on less effective products. 2. What is the campaign naming convention? How do we structure campaign names? (2 marks) Ans. The Campaign Naming Convention follows a structured format to clearly identify and categorize each campaign based on specific parameters: Product Code: This is a unique code or abbreviation representing the product being advertised. For example, "HBR" might stand for "Hydrolyte Blue Razz." Ad Type: Indicates the type of Amazon ad being used: "SP" for Sponsored Product "SB" for Sponsored Brand "SD" for Sponsored Display Match Type: Specifies the targeting match type used for keywords or product targeting: "Auto" for automatic targeting (includes close match, loose match, complements, substitutes) "Exact" for exact match targeting "Phrases" for phrase match targeting "Broad" for broad match targeting "Product Targeting" for campaigns targeting specific products or categories Purpose: Describes the strategic purpose of the campaign, such as: "Ranking KW" for campaigns aimed at improving keyword rankings "Branded KW" for campaigns targeting branded keywords "Defensive" for campaigns aimed at defending against competitors "Competitors" for campaigns targeting competitor keywords Source: Indicates where the keyword or targeting data originates from: "Helium 10" for data sourced from Helium 10 keyword research "STR" for data sourced from Search Term Report "Amz KW" for keywords sourced from Amazon's own keyword suggestions or data Number: A numerical identifier used to differentiate campaigns and avoid duplications. This number can help organize campaigns based on the number of keywords or targets included in each campaign. Example Campaign Name: "HBR - SP - Exact - Ranking KW - Helium 10 - 01" "HBR": Product Code (Hydrolyte Blue Razz) "SP": Ad Type (Sponsored Product) "Exact": Match Type (Exact match targeting) "Ranking KW": Purpose (Campaign aimed at ranking keywords) "Helium 10": Source (Keyword data sourced from Helium 10) "01": Number (First campaign for this specific purpose and source) 3. Explain the three different campaign bidding strategies? Which one do we use by default? (3 marks) Ans. Fixed Bids - With fixed bids, advertisers manually set a specific bid amount for each keyword or targeting option within the campaign. The bid remains constant regardless of the keyword's performance or competition level. Dynamic Bids - Down Only - allows Amazon to automatically lower your bid for clicks that are less likely to result in a sale. This strategy is suitable for advertisers who want to maximize clicks within a given budget while minimizing spending on less valuable clicks. Dynamic Bids - Up and Down - enables Amazon to automatically adjust bids both up and down based on the likelihood of conversion. Amazon increases bids for clicks that are more likely to lead to sales and decreases bids for less likely conversions. This strategy helps advertisers maximize conversion opportunities while optimizing ad spend efficiently. ● The default bidding strategy we utilize is Dynamic Bids - Down Only, which allows us to optimize bids for the targets within a campaign, regardless of their performance. This strategy prevents excessive spending when our bids are lower, unlike strategies based on fixed bids or specific placements. 4. Explain each of the four auto campaign targeting types? (4 marks) Ans. Close Match: In Close Match targeting, Amazon matches your ad to search queries that are closely related to your product. This includes searches where the user's intent closely matches the product you are advertising. Close Match targeting capture a broad range of relevant search queries that are directly related to your product's category. Loose Match: Loose Match targeting is broader than Close Match and includes a wider range of search queries that may be loosely related to your product. This targeting type allows Amazon to display your ad for search queries that might not directly match your product but are still within a relevant category. It helps reach a larger audience and can capture customers with varied search behavior. Complements: Complements targeting focuses
